preconditions.description: n is the number of crimes (0 ≤ n ≤ 10¹⁸) and c is the number of conditions (0 ≤ c ≤ 1000).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= m <= 123 for (t, m) in conditions) and len(set(t for t, m in conditions)) <= 26
preconditions.description: Each condition consists of a crime type (capital Latin letter) and a positive integer multiplicity (1 ≤ m ≤ 123). The product of all multiplicities does not exceed 123, and there are at most 26 unique crime types.

preconditions.expression: conditions == [] or all(isinstance(t, str) and len(t) == 1 and t.isupper() for t, m in conditions)
preconditions.description: Each crime type is a single uppercase Latin letter.
If n and c are provided, the first line is 'n c'; if n=0 and c=0, input is empty (edge case).

postconditions.description: Output is a non-negative integer modulo 12345 representing the number of valid sequences.

postconditions.expression: crime_types := {t for t, m in conditions} and len(crime_types) == 0 == (n == 0)
postconditions.description: If no crime types are listed (c=0), the only valid sequence is the empty sequence (n=0).

postconditions.expression: all(t in crime_types for t in sequence) and len(sequence) == n and all(count(sequence, t) % m == 0 for t, m in conditions if count(sequence, t) > 0)
postconditions.description: For each valid sequence of length n, every crime type in the sequence must be in crime_types, and for each crime type t with multiplicity m, the count of t in the sequence must be a multiple of m (or zero).

postconditions.expression: count_sequences := sum(1 for sequence in product(crime_types, repeat=n) if all(count(sequence, t) % m == 0 for t, m in conditions if count(sequence, t) > 0)) and int(stdout.strip()) == count_sequences % 12345
postconditions.description: The output is the count of all valid sequences of length n modulo 12345, where a sequence is valid if it meets the multiplicity conditions for all crime types.

postconditions.expression: crime_types == set() == (n == 0) or (n > 0 and crime_types != set())
postconditions.description: If n > 0, at least one crime type must be provided (c > 0).
